COMET spatial PLA analysis: Codex implementation
instructions
Scope: initial spatial running-minus-homecage difference maps, reusing the previously completed tissue alignment
and existing tissue masks. These are instructions, not analysis results.
1. Deliverables and comparisons
• Generate two primary spatial difference heatmaps: TDP43-HK1 (Running − Homecage) and TDP43-PFKP
 (Running − Homecage). Keep the two PLA types fully separate throughout processing.
• Regenerate the same alignment-check figure used previously, so the previously accepted tissue
 alignment can be inspected visually. Do not recalculate or change the alignment.
• Generate spatial coverage maps that show, for each aligned bin, the number of tissue sections
 contributing to that bin’s average, separately for Running and Homecage for each PLA type (four maps
total, or equivalently clearly labeled panels).
2. Alignment and shared bin grid
• Reuse the pre-existing coordinate transformations, anatomical orientation, reference space, and
 tissue-section alignment. Never realign sections in this implementation.
• In the common aligned x,y coordinate space, establish identical grid boundaries and bin dimensions for
 all included sections and both conditions. Reuse the existing grid if available; otherwise make bin
dimensions configurable and record them.
• Assign each PLA object to the bin containing its aligned centroid. Count each object once. Determine
 counts at the individual-section level before averaging.
3. Tissue validity: strict 100% coverage rule
• Reuse each section’s existing tissue outline/mask, transformed into the same aligned coordinate space
 as the PLA centroids and spatial grid. Do not infer tissue coverage from PLA signals or create a new
mask unless specifically requested.
• For any bin and any section, mark that section valid only if 100% of the entire bin area lies within that
 section’s existing tissue mask/boundary. If any portion extends outside the tissue outline, exclude that
section from that bin’s calculation.
• If the entire bin is inside the tissue mask but contains no PLA centroid, its count is 0 and that zero must
 contribute to the mean. Missing tissue must never be coded as zero PLA.
• Use the same full-bin inclusion test consistently across sections; handle boundary geometry and raster
 masks conservatively, without rounding a partially covered bin up to fully covered. A bin is displayable
in a difference map only if at least one valid section contributes in both conditions.
4. Spatial averaging and difference calculation
For each PLA type, spatial bin b, and condition c, let V(c,b) be the set of sections whose tissue masks fully
contain bin b. Let P(s,b) be the count of PLA centroids in that bin for section s, including valid zeros.
Calculate:
Mean(c,b) = [sum of P(s,b) for s in V(c,b)] / [number of sections in V(c,b)]
Difference(b) = Mean(Running,b) − Mean(Homecage,b)

2
Example: Homecage counts 3, 5, 4 → mean 4; Running counts 7, 8, 9 → mean 8; difference = +4 for that
spatial bin. Sections excluded by the tissue-coverage rule do not enter either numerator or denominator.
5. Plotting requirements
• Produce the two difference heatmaps on the original aligned x,y grid with the preserved anatomical
 orientation. Plot positive values as higher mean counts in Running and negative values as lower mean
counts in Running.
• Use a diverging colormap centered at zero with identical symmetric color limits across both PLA types.
 Show bins with insufficient coverage in either condition as missing/masked, visually distinct from bins
with zero difference.
• Label the color bar: Difference in mean PLA count per spatial bin (Running − Homecage). Do not
 smooth, interpolate, normalize, or run statistical tests in this initial version.
6. Validation data and files to save
• Save the two primary difference heatmaps, the reproduced alignment check, and the four
 condition-specific spatial coverage maps (or a clearly labeled multi-panel equivalent).
• Save the numerical homecage mean, running mean, difference, and valid-section-count matrices for
 every PLA type; also retain the tissue-validity matrix for each section and the recorded
grid/mask/alignment parameters.
• Preserve section IDs, animal IDs, condition, PLA type, and source-file identifiers so values are traceable
 back to actual consolidated object-level HALO/COMET data and the existing alignment/masks. Do not
use previously derived summary plots as analytical inputs.
7. Code organization and first-pass acceptance checks
• Keep alignment, grid/bin assignment, mask-based validity, per-section counts, averaging, and condition
 comparison as separate steps/functions. Future analyses will change the comparison math while
reusing the spatial infrastructure.
• Confirm by inspection that the alignment-check figure matches the previous accepted alignment.
 Confirm that zero-PLA but fully covered bins contribute zeros; bins even slightly outside a section mask
do not contribute; and section-count maps match each condition’s actual number of eligible sections.
• Verify that each displayed difference equals its corresponding Running mean minus Homecage mean,
 and that HK1/PFKP are never pooled.
